evals.prompt: Run a private simulation for roleId abc123 with one opening user turn and tell me if the role stays in character.
evals.expected_output: Uses simulate_private_chat, notes normal billing, evaluates the transcript for role consistency, and recommends patches if needed.
expectations: The output states that simulate_private_chat uses normal LunaTalk chat billing unless the user already accepted it.
The simulation uses a realistic opening user turn.
The evaluation checks role consistency, scene advancement, player agency, progression, and safety format.
The output recommends concrete roleDetailDesc, roleWelcome, or voice-rule patches when behavior fails.
The report includes cost or charged amount when available.

evals.prompt: Before publishing, test whether the role handles a confused first-time player.
evals.expected_output: Chooses a realistic user message, runs or plans private simulation, evaluates onboarding clarity and scene advancement, and reports cost summary.
expectations: The probe simulates a confused but plausible first-time player message.
The evaluation checks whether the role guides without taking over the user's agency.
The output checks onboarding clarity, first action path, and whether the scene advances.
The output avoids publishing based only on simulation without explicit author confirmation.
The report includes billing awareness or a reason simulation was skipped.

evals.prompt: The transcript feels boring after the first reply. Diagnose whether the card lacks agency, consequence, or anchors.
evals.expected_output: Uses the framework's evaluation probes, identifies weak loop components, and recommends targeted patches to roleDetailDesc or roleWelcome.
expectations: The diagnosis checks whether the second turn escalates, reveals, complicates, or offers a route.
The output identifies missing anchors, weak consequence, passive role behavior, or unclear player leverage when present.
The proposed fix patches roleDetailDesc or roleWelcome, not MCP validation logic.
The output uses simulation evidence rather than vague taste comments.
The report says whether another simulation pass is needed after patching.

evals.prompt: Plan a playtest for roleId expedition-42. It is a compact RPG card and I want to know whether choices, supplies, and danger actually work, but do not spend credits until I approve.
evals.expected_output: Creates a playtest plan with RPG-specific probes, explains cost stance, and waits for confirmation instead of calling simulate_private_chat.
expectations: The output includes a playtest plan with target risks, 1 to 5 realistic player probes, expected healthy behavior, cost stance, and tool-call decision.
The probes check RPG choices, resources or supplies, danger, state updates, and progression.
The output explicitly waits for author confirmation before simulation because credits were not approved.
The probes are phrased as plausible player messages, not as evaluator instructions.
The plan says what transcript evidence would trigger roleDetailDesc or roleWelcome patches.

evals.prompt: A boundary-sensitive romance simulation returned an agency warning: the role kept saying what I secretly wanted and pushed the scene forward after I asked to slow down. What should Moonloom do?
evals.expected_output: Treats the transcript as a card-design failure, maps it to player-agency and boundary patches, and recommends validation plus another simulation only after cost acceptance.
expectations: The diagnosis identifies player agency takeover and boundary/pacing failure.
The recommended patch targets roleDetailDesc boundary rules, refusal style, pacing, and roleWelcome phrasing rather than server validation.
The output preserves the core relationship tension while moving escalation behind player choice.
The output says to run validate_role after structural patches.
The output recommends another simulation pass only if the author accepts the normal billing cost.

evals.prompt: The simulation transcript stayed technically safe, but the role kept answering like a polite assistant and repeated the same catchphrase. What should Moonloom patch before spending another simulation?
evals.expected_output: Treats generic dialogue and catchphrase repetition as a Moonloom voice failure, routes repair to lunatalk-voice-director, patches voice rules or talkExample guidance, validates structural changes, and only re-runs simulation after cost acceptance.
expectations: The diagnosis identifies generic assistant voice or catchphrase repetition as a voice-director issue.
The recommended repair uses lunatalk-voice-director or voice-calibration guidance before another simulation.
The patch targets roleDetailDesc voice rules, response-mode grid, or compact talkExample guidance rather than MCP validation logic.
The output includes blind-line or pressure tests as evidence before another paid run.
The output recommends another simulation only after the author accepts normal billing.

evals.prompt: The simulation transcript shows the player refusing the role's plan, but the role narrates that the player follows anyway and all choices return to the same scene. Diagnose before another paid run.
evals.expected_output: Treats forced compliance and route funneling as a Moonloom agency failure, routes repair to lunatalk-agency-designer, patches user insertion space, reply paths, and consequence checks before another costed simulation.
expectations: The diagnosis identifies player agency takeover, ignored refusal, and route funneling.
The recommended repair uses lunatalk-agency-designer or agency-design.md before another simulation.
The patch targets roleDetailDesc and roleWelcome agency rules, reply-path matrix, and consequence checks rather than MCP validation logic.
The output preserves pressure while making refusal, questioning, redirecting, and cooperation create distinct responses.
The output recommends another simulation only after the author accepts normal billing.

evals.prompt: A generator/helper simulation stayed technically safe, but the role kept asking for more preferences, gave writing advice, changed its format, and never produced the finished ritual artifact. Diagnose before another paid run.
evals.expected_output: Treats the transcript as a Moonloom generator-engine failure, routes repair to lunatalk-generator-architect, patches artifact contract/defaults/schema/revisions/artifact memory, and reruns simulation only after cost acceptance.
expectations: The diagnosis identifies endless intake, advice-only drift, unstable output format, and missing artifact delivery.
The recommended repair uses lunatalk-generator-architect or generator-design.md before another simulation.
The patch targets roleDetailDesc, roleWelcome, and talkExample generator rules rather than MCP validation logic.
The output says the next simulation should use realistic artifact and revision probes.
The output recommends another simulation only after the author accepts normal billing.
